plan_a_advantages: More frequent trail running sessions build trail-specific endurance.
The repeated easy recovery runs support consistent training and prevent overtraining.
The longer endurance run (120 minutes) provides a significant stimulus for building aerobic capacity.

reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It prioritizes consistent, moderate-paced trail running, which is crucial for building the aerobic base and trail-specific endurance necessary for speed. Plan B, while including cross-training and strength work, focuses heavily on low-intensity, shorter runs and a single longer run, which doesn't provide the volume needed for significant speed development. Plan A’s repeated easy recovery runs and longer endurance runs will build the necessary fatigue resistance and mileage to support faster paces, whereas Plan B’s emphasis on low-impact and controlled effort may not translate to the sustained effort required for faster trail running.
